equation_request.abstract: We construct a classical algorithm that designs quantum circuits for algorithmic quantum simulation of arbitrary qudit channels on fault-tolerant quantum computers within a pre-specified error tolerance with respect to diamond-norm distance. The classical algorithm is constructed by decomposing a quantum channel into a convex combination of generalized extreme channels by optimization of a set of nonlinear coupled algebraïc equations. The resultant circuit is a randomly chosen generalized extreme channel circuit whose run-time is logarithmic with respect to the error tolerance and quadratic with respect to Hilbert space dimension, which requires only a single ancillary qudit plus classical dits.

specification.problem: Classically design quantum circuits that simulate an arbitrary qudit channel on a fault-tolerant quantum computer within a prescribed diamond-norm error, by decomposing the channel into a convex combination of generalized extreme channels and randomly sampling one such channel circuit.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the decomposition and sampling framework only; the nonlinear coupled equations, circuit construction, measurement details, and gate-level details are not given in the abstract.

specification.initial_state: System in arbitrary input state rho; ancilla qudit in a fixed reference state (assumed |0>); classical dits initialized to 0.

steps.description: Classically solve the nonlinear coupled algebraic equations to decompose the target channel into weights p_k and generalized extreme channels E_k, to within tolerance epsilon.
Randomly sample an index k with probability p_k.
Apply the fault-tolerant circuit implementing the sampled generalized extreme channel E_k on the system plus the single ancilla qudit, using classical dits as needed.
Discard or reset the ancilla; the averaged output is the simulated channel within epsilon in diamond norm.

specification.measurement: No measurement is specified in the abstract. The output is the channel's output state on the system register, with the ancilla discarded. Any mid-circuit measurement or classical-dit recording inside a generalized extreme channel circuit is unspecified. Assumed: the user measures the system in whatever basis their downstream task requires.
